title: Lamps on the tower
description: The signal tower shows numbers with a row of lamps. Read them, and set them, in binary.

tasks.title: Every number can be written with just 0 and 1
tasks.body: In binary each place is worth twice the place to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and so on. 1101 means one 8, one 4, no 2 and one 1, which is 13. A computer stores every number this way, as a row of bits, each one on or off.
tasks.detail: To read binary from the left, start at 0 and, for each bit, double what you have and add the bit. To write a number in binary, take n % 2 for the last bit, then n // 2, and repeat until nothing is left. Python can do both with bin() and int(text, 2), but working it out by hand is what this lesson is about.

tasks.code:
# The tower shows numbers with lamps: on is 1, off is 0
lamps = "1101"
value = 0
for lamp in lamps:
    value = value * 2 + int(lamp)
print(value)
print(bin(13))
print(int("1101", 2))
tasks.note: Reading 1101 from the left: 0 doubled plus 1 is 1, then 3, then 6, then 13. bin() writes 13 with a 0b in front to say it is binary, and int(..., 2) reads binary text back.

tasks.question: What is the binary 10010 as an ordinary number?

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: change the lamps to "11111111" and work out the value first. Then print bin(255) and compare.

Write to_binary(n), which returns the binary of a whole number n (0 or more) as text, like "1101" for 13 and "0" for 0, without a 0b in front. Then write from_binary(bits), which takes text such as "1101" and returns the number, 13. Try it with // and % before reaching for bin(). Do not ask for input: the check calls your functions with its own values.
hints: For to_binary(), the last bit is n % 2. Then n // 2 shifts everything one place right. Repeat while n is more than 0, putting each new bit in front of the ones you have.
For from_binary(), go through the text from the left: double the value so far, then add the bit, int(bit). 0 needs its own answer in to_binary(), because the loop never runs for it.
With other names, for base 3: digits = str(k % 3) + digits, then k = k // 3, inside a while loop.

error_hints.text: Use the parameter names from each def line, spelled the same way.
Text and numbers do not mix: str() turns a bit into text to join, and int() turns a "1" into the number 1.
to_binary(13) should return "1101": 13 % 2 is 1, then 6 % 2 is 0, then 3 % 2 is 1, then 1 % 2 is 1, read from last to first.
to_binary(0) should return "0": the loop never runs for 0, so give it its own answer.
from_binary("1101") should return 13: double, then add the bit, from the left.
Check text that starts with 0s: they add nothing.

similar_example.code:
def to_base3(k):
    digits = ""
    while k > 0:
        digits = str(k % 3) + digits
        k = k // 3
    return digits

print(to_base3(10))
similar_example.note: The same idea in base 3, where each place is worth three times the one to its right. Your lamps use base 2, and 0 needs care.

other_ways.note: Python's own tools: bin() gives "0b1101", and [2:] cuts off the 0b. Now you know what they do inside.
to_binary() calling itself on a smaller number, which the recursion unit explains, and from_binary() adding up the place values from the right.
